rationale: The matching holds. I tested all 24 row and token pairs. The knowledge base search page is hosted as a web resource: the out-of-the-box Knowledge Search template has application type Web Resource, and the create-template example pairs a knowledge base search page with Web resource. Search takes searchType 0 for relevance search and a searchText slug such as {anchor.title}. Entity record opens a create form, and its data parameter prefills the subject, as in the page's {anchor.ticketnumber} example. Entity list displays a view selected by viewId. Third-party website and Custom fit no row. Check 21 passes, because row 1 turns on a fact the names mislead about: the natural pick for a search page is Search. Dashboard is a page type that isn't a token, and it fits no row. The defect is one false sentence in an option explanation.
findings: False statement in option d's explanation. "A web resource tab doesn't run a Dataverse relevance search or display an entity view" is contradicted by row 1 itself: the knowledge base search web resource runs knowledge searches, and Learn sets no such limit on web resources. Fix: replace that sentence with "A web resource tab opens the file that webresourceName names, and it doesn't take the searchType, searchText or viewId parameters."

rationale: All four rows are right, and I tested every row against every token. Row 4 avoids the page's parent and child conflict: it relies only on Clone input record taking Entity record ID and Entity logical name and not saving, against Clone current record cloning the record open in the current tab. Save the record and Clone current record fit no row. The defect is check 21.
findings: Check 21. Every row maps to the token whose name describes it: change a field on an existing record to Update an existing record, fill in fields to Autofill form fields, start a new form to Open a new form to create a record, and copy another case by its ID to Clone input record rather than Clone current record. No row turns on a fact the names don't give. Fix: make row 1 turn on the save behaviour. Row r1 label: "Change the priority of the case open in the focused tab, with the new value saved by that action alone" (correctTokenId stays a). Answer: replace "Related account: Update an existing record." with "Case priority: Update an existing record." Explanation: replace "so it suits an account that isn't open." with "so the new priority is saved without a form save." Option a explanation: "Correct for the case priority. It needs the entity logical name and record ID, and it updates the record as a back-end operation, so the change is saved without a form save. It can't fill a new task that has no record ID yet." Option b explanation: "Correct for the focused task form. It applies to the form in the focused tab with the same entity type and doesn't save the values until the form autosaves, so on row 1 it would change the case form without saving the priority." Option c explanation: "Fails on every row. It clones the record that's open in the current tab. Row 4 copies another case that the macro knows only by its ID, and no other row copies a record." After the fix, the names point row 1 at Autofill form fields, because the case form is in focus, or at Save the record, because of the word saved. Only the documented facts that Autofill doesn't save until the form autosaves and that Update an existing record writes as a back-end operation settle it, and no other token becomes valid on any row.

Clone current record clones the record open in the current tab; Clone input record takes record ID and logical name; neither saves. The clone examples contradict themselves on parent and child, which the rows avoid.

rationale: Rows 1 to 3 are right. findings: Checks 5 and 9. Token e is rejected only because Advanced settings are "documented for the conversation record type". The same page's custom view procedure says that for each record type you choose Simple or Advanced, and that Advanced builds your own conditions when the simple filters don't cover the scenario, so a learner can reasonably believe an Advanced email view could filter on the To field. Fix: token e text: "Add a custom view that uses the Emails assigned to me setting". Option e explanation: "Fails. This setting shows emails whose Owner or Worked by field is the current user. It doesn't target the claims address." In the explanation, replace "and Advanced settings are documented for the conversation record type." with "and Emails assigned to me depends on the email's Owner or Worked by field." In the sim-cb-s14 evidence claim, add: "Emails assigned to me shows emails whose Owner or Worked by field is the current user." In duplicateCheck, replace "Sort and Advanced settings appear only as distractors." with "Sort and Emails assigned to me appear only as distractors." The new token is a simple setting listed for Email on both pages, it fits no row, and it keeps tokens c, d and e parallel.

rationale: All four rows are right, and I tested every row against every token. The role privilege lets everyone with the role disconnect chats on any record type. Record owner can disconnect chats covers chats on owned records, including ones a colleague connected. Join chat needs write access, which the stem states. Status is preconfigured for case key updates. The stem's default sentence covers every toggle option, so under check 32 it marks none. The defect is check 21.
findings: Check 21. Each row maps to the token whose name describes it: quality leads to the one token that names the quality leads' role, a case's owner to Record owner can disconnect chats, entering connected chats to Join chat, and being told about a status change to Receive notification on key updates. No row turns on a fact the names don't give. Fix: make row 3 turn on the documented limit of the timeline sync preview. Row r3 label: "A representative who takes over a case can read the full message history of the chats already connected to it" (correctTokenId stays d). In the explanation, after the sentence ending "such as a case they've taken over.", add: "The timeline sync preview shows only who connected each chat and who sent the last message, so reading the whole chat still depends on joining it." Option d explanation: "Correct for a representative who takes over a case. Join chat lets users view and join connected chats on records they have write access to, and joining shows the full chat exchange. It's set per record type." Option f explanation: "Fails on every row. This preview setting shows each connected chat on the record's timeline, with who connected it and who sent the last message. Reading the full exchange still needs Join chat, and the setting doesn't send field updates or grant disconnect rights." In the sim-d5-s08 evidence claim, add: "The timeline entry shows who connected the chat and when, and the last person to send a message and when." After the fix, the names point row 3 at the sync setting, and only the documented split between the timeline entry and joining settles it.

rationale: Stands. Every neighbouring pair is a state dependency on the current page. Save and close leaves the provider Inactive with status reason Validated, the only state where a trial ingestion runs, and Save as draft blocks all ingestion. The trial must come before activation, because it needs an inactive, validated provider and because activation starts ingestion and puts articles in search results, which the first requirement forbids before the check. Time-range ingestion needs Active with Ingestion Ready, and the page says to activate first. Check 1 reverse search: I searched Learn for integrated search provider pages and opened View and use insights for search providers, the Insights troubleshooting article and the msdyn_integratedsearchprovider table reference. None shows another order, and the table reference confirms that Ingestion Ready is the only Active status reason, while Validated and Draft are Inactive. The 30-day range is inside the 60-day limit. Both distractors fail for documented reasons. The evidence notes are accurate.

Activation starts ingestion and articles start appearing in search results. Filters work only with Dataverse search. Site map needs lastmod; static sites only.

rationale: Rows 2 and 3 hold: setting a custom profile as the default removes its existing security roles, and a custom default doesn't apply to users assigned specific custom profiles. On row 1 I applied checks 4, 5 and 9. Learn doesn't describe what Set as default does while another default exists, but it says you can't set multiple profiles as the default and that to change the default you use Remove Default and then set the alternative profile. I treat that procedure as a documented requirement, so the automatic swap fails for a documented reason rather than for silence. Check 5: the FAQ agrees that admin center can't produce two defaults, and its exception for imported profiles doesn't apply here. Check 4 holds, because the row asks what the change requires, not which default to pick. Distinct from sim-c-q05, which fixes two defaults created by an import. The defect is the wording of row 1.
findings: Check 23. Row 1's answer heading is Expected behavior, and the correct option is the only one written as an instruction ("Remove Default from Legacy Desk first"), while both distractors describe outcomes, which marks it. Fix: r1a text: "Legacy Desk's default has to be removed first". r1b text: "Legacy Desk's default is removed automatically". r1c unchanged. r1b explanation: "Fails. You can't set multiple profiles as the default, and Microsoft's procedure for changing it is to use Remove Default on the current default and then set the alternative profile."

rationale: Stands. findings: Checks 16 and 22. The requirements clear every distractor by wording alone.
